authority: meaning_ja selects the target sense/use; canonical answer determines grammarRole. paraphrases[] is semantic-equivalence authority and does not determine grammarRole.

rules.rule: Multiword lexical verbs, including phrasal and prepositional verbs, are verb.
Multiword prepositions are preposition when the complete expression heads a relation and takes its complement.
Multiword conjunctions are conjunction when they connect clauses or constituents.
Semi-modals are auxiliary only when they share modal/auxiliary grammatical function for the prompt; lexical predicates stay verb.
Pronoun versus determiner follows the specified use in meaning_ja; pronominal heads are not merged into noun.
Predicative adjective expressions may include be; classify the predicate complement function as adjective when canonical and paraphrases share it.
Independent conventional reactions/responses are interjection only when the accepted answer set shares that discourse-response use.
Construction is reserved for a reusable multi-slot or word-order template; an ordinary phrase or a complete fixed clause is not automatically construction.
Paraphrase POS differences do not affect grammarRole. Resolve from the canonical answer under meaning_ja; use pending only for a genuinely unresolved canonical usage.

A surface fragment may be classified by its syntactic function when the prompt supplies it (e.g. predicate adjective, adverbial, NP); utterance pragmatics alone does not override form unless the entry is a conventional standalone reaction.

Construction is used when a fixed syntactic frame itself carries the learning target and open slots are central; examples include the comparative-correlative, chances are (that) S, be yet to do, and not only A but also B.
when it comes to X and as far as X is concerned are conjunctions in the specified topic-setting use.
Auxiliary is limited to productive modal or semi-modal operators assigning possibility, obligation, intention, necessity, or imminence to a following VP; a fixed be yet to do frame is construction.
A standalone conventional discourse act/response is interjection, including no problem, why not?, be my guest, so much for X, there you go again, and small-talk what’s up.
A canonical quantified expression with no following noun functions as pronoun; when it precedes a noun and restricts its quantity it functions as determiner.

The confirmed prompt is （君主の）治世; canonical reign is the noun sense.

superseded_ledger_notes.reason: be eager to do something is an adjective predicate, while long to do something is a lexical verb predicate; the accepted answer set does not share one grammatical role.
It's on me is a clause with a prepositional predicate; my treat is a noun phrase. The Japanese payment-response meaning does not make their grammatical roles identical.
be on someone’s side is a predicative prepositional/adjectival complement, while side with someone is a lexical verb phrase; the accepted answer set does not share one grammatical role.
differ from something is a lexical verb predicate, while be different from something is an adjective predicate. Both express the prompt meaning but do not share one grammatical role.
go along with and support are verb phrases, but be in favor of something is a predicative adjective/prepositional phrase. The accepted answer set spans roles.
despite and in spite of take noun phrase complements (prepositions), while although and even though introduce clauses (conjunctions). The accepted answer set crosses the boundary.
be dying of thirst is a verbal predicate, while be parched is a predicative adjective. The answer set has no shared role.
so much for something is a discourse-level closing formula, while leave it at that is a lexical verb clause. The prompt does not align these to one shared grammatical category.
be faced with is a participial/adjectival predicate in this state meaning, while face and be confronted with are verbal predicates. The accepted forms do not establish a single role.
be jealous of someone is an adjective predicate, while envy someone is a lexical verb. The accepted answer set crosses categories.
the canonical is a comparative-correlative multi-clause pattern; practice makes perfect is a fixed declarative clause, not the same reusable construction. No single allowed role covers both forms.
time will tell is a complete fixed assertion, not a reusable slot template; the taxonomy has no clause/sentence category, and no paraphrase provides a shared narrower role.
have one’s hands full is a verb predicate, while be tied up is an adjective/participial predicate. The answer set crosses categories.
You flatter me and You’re flattering me share the lexical verb predicate flatter; standalone conversational use does not alter their common grammar role.
no sooner...than and hardly...when are multi-slot correlative inversion patterns; classify the entry by this paired clause pattern, despite the as soon as conjunction paraphrase.
and so on / and so forth / et cetera extend a coordinated list; classify their shared list-coordination function.
a piece of cake and child’s play are noun phrases denoting an easy task.
leave nothing to be desired is a lexical verb phrase, while perfect is an adjective. They share the “excellent” meaning but not a grammatical role.
call for / need / require are lexical verbs, while be in need of something is a predicative adjective phrase. The accepted answer set crosses categories.
be interested in is an adjective predicate; have an interest in is a lexical verb phrase. Same prompt meaning, different grammatical roles.
such as and like take noun phrase complements as prepositions, while for example is an adverbial. The accepted set has no single role.
go on a diet and diet are verbal predicates, while be on a diet is a state predicate with an adjectival complement. The accepted set crosses roles.
envy someone is a lexical verb, while be envious of someone is an adjective predicate.
count and matter are lexical verbs; be important and be significant are adjective predicates. The accepted set does not share one category.
be on good terms is a predicative phrase, while get along/get on are lexical verb predicates. The accepted set crosses categories.
be my guest is a conventional permission response, but go ahead and please include imperative verb forms; these do not share a grammatical role.
hold on/hang on are imperative verbs; just a moment/wait a second include a noun phrase. The shared request meaning does not determine one grammatical category.
rather than can connect clauses or constituents, while instead of is a preposition taking a noun/gerund complement. The Japanese gloss does not disambiguate complement type.
be tied up is a participial/adjectival predicate; have your hands full is a lexical verb predicate. The answer set crosses roles.
be lost is an adjective/state predicate, while have lost your way is a perfect-tense verb predicate. No single role is shared.
there’s no use doing / there’s no point in doing are existential noun constructions, while it’s pointless to do is an adjective clause. The answer set has different structures and roles.
in time is an adverbial phrase, while make it in time is a verb clause. The answer set does not share one grammatical role.
not only A but also B is a paired multi-slot construction, whereas A as well as B is a coordinating conjunction phrase. The accepted set crosses the construction/conjunction boundary.
be abundant/rich in is an adjective predicate; abound in is a lexical verb. The answer set crosses categories.
not so much X as Y is a balanced focus/contrast template whose constituent slots and parallel ordering are the learning target.
can’t help doing and can’t resist doing share the negated modal can’s inability/avoidance force; classify by the modal function for this prompt.
back and forth expresses direction/frequency of movement as an adverbial, not an action predicate.
come close to doing / almost do / nearly do are all verbal predicates in the target infinitive frame; almost/nearly modify the lexical verb internally.
watch out/look out are imperative lexical verb predicates, while be careful is an adjective predicate. The response meaning does not make the accepted forms share one grammatical role.
chances are is a complete clause, while probably is an adverb. Both express likelihood but the prompt does not define a common grammatical role.
have something to do with is a lexical verb phrase; be related to is an adjective predicate. The answer set crosses roles.
be attributed to is a passive verbal predicate, while be due to is an adjective predicate. They do not share one grammatical category.
come in handy is a lexical verb predicate, while be useful is an adjective predicate.
close at hand is an adjective phrase; within easy reach is a prepositional phrase. The prompt gives a state/location meaning but does not select one role.
under construction is a prepositional state phrase, while be being built is a passive verb clause. The accepted set crosses roles.
be in danger of doing is an adjective predicate, while risk doing is a lexical verb predicate.

at the latest is an adverbial phrase, while no later than takes a time complement as a complex preposition. The answer set does not share one category; this same contrast is added to the cross-batch rule ledger.

all someone has to do is do something is a multi-slot focus construction; someone only has to do something is a semi-modal auxiliary pattern. The accepted set spans the template and auxiliary functions.
be free of is an adjective predicate, while not contain something is a lexical verb predicate.
what’s going on / what’s happening are complete interrogative clauses rather than a single lexical category. The taxonomy has no sentence class and these are not clearly a slot template.
feel like doing is a lexical verb phrase; be in the mood to do is an adjective predicate. The accepted answer set crosses roles.
no later than takes a time complement as a complex preposition, while at the latest is adverbial; shared time-limit meaning does not establish one role.
The canonical and paraphrases are all conventional standalone replies to thanks; classify their shared discourse-response function as interjection despite syntactic variation.
against someone’s will is headed by the preposition against and takes a noun-phrase complement; its phrase-level adverbial use does not change its category.
be confronted with / be faced with both express a stative condition through participial adjective predicates.
how often / how frequently are interrogative adverb phrases asking about frequency, not a separate question category.
as many as / no fewer than quantify an ensuing nominal quantity; function is determiner/quantifier.
contribute to / play a part in are verb predicates, but be a factor in something is a noun predicate. Their contribution meaning does not give one shared grammatical role.
at all costs is an adverbial phrase, while whatever it takes is a free relative clause. They share a resolve-at-any-price meaning, not a grammatical category.
would rather do is a modal auxiliary plus bare infinitive preference construction, while prefer doing is a lexical verb predicate. The answer set crosses auxiliary/verb function.
stand by someone is a lexical verb phrase, while be there for someone is a predicative locative/adjectival phrase. The accepted set has no shared role.
be up to someone is a predicative phrase; depend on someone is a lexical verb predicate. The prompt does not align their grammatical roles.
in the face of something is a preposition phrase, while faced with something is a participial adjective/passive predicate. The answer set crosses categories.
deserve praise is a lexical verb, while commendable and be worthy of praise are adjective predicates.
there you go again / here we go again are complete fixed clauses used as discourse reactions, not a reusable slot template with one lexical category.
be a must has a noun complement, while be essential / indispensable are adjective predicates. The answer set crosses categories.
feel free to do is an adjective predicate, while don’t hesitate to do is an imperative verb clause. Their permission meaning does not give one shared role.
may well do uses a modal auxiliary, while have good reason to do is a lexical verb predicate. The accepted set crosses auxiliary/verb function.

be far from is an adjective predicate with a prepositional complement; nowhere near is a prepositional phrase and a far cry from is a noun phrase. The prompt does not resolve a shared grammatical role.
be obliged to / have no choice but to / be forced to share an obligation/necessity operator function at prompt level; treated as semi-modal auxiliary in this taxonomy.
the time is ripe / the time is right share the same predicative adjective function for maturity/readiness.
if only + clause / I wish + clause are reusable multi-slot wish templates, and the template is the learning target.
required / necessary / needed for something function as state/property predicates in this meaning.
mind your own business / stay out of it share imperative lexical verb predicates.
there’s no point/use + gerund is a reusable slot construction; both accepted answers share that existential template.
behind someone’s back / without someone knowing / without someone’s knowledge introduce NP or gerund complements as prepositional expressions.
be forced to / have no choice but to / be obliged to share a necessity/obligation function at prompt level; treated as semi-modal auxiliary.
The canonical tend to do is a lexical verb; be inclined to is an adjective predicate; have a tendency to is a noun phrase predicate. The answer set has no shared grammatical role.
be concerned with is an adjective predicate in this focus sense, while focus on/center on/deal with are lexical verb predicates.
be involved in is an adjective/stative participial predicate; take part in/participate in are lexical verbs.
come to light is a lexical verb phrase, while become clear/apparent are copular adjective predicates.
when it comes to is a subordinate clause frame; as for/regarding/with regard to are prepositional expressions and as far as ... is concerned is a clause.
be capable of is an adjective predicate, be able to is semi-modal, and have the ability to is a noun-headed verb phrase.
nothing but/nothing more than is a pronoun/determiner phrase; be merely something is a clause with merely modifying the predicate.
what will become/happen to us are complete interrogative clauses, not a single lexical category or a clear reusable slot template.
at any moment/any minute now are adverbials, while be about to do is a semi-modal auxiliary construction.
in favor of is a prepositional phrase; support/back are lexical verbs.
correspond/match/agree are lexical verbs, while be consistent with is an adjective predicate.
in sight/within sight are prepositional phrases, while visible is an adjective; prompt does not privilege one category.
so as not to/in order not to introduce purpose infinitives, while to avoid doing is a lexical verb phrase.
in search of is a prepositional phrase; look for/seek are lexical verbs.
believe it or not is an imperative parenthetical; you may not believe this, but is a clause coordinated with but.
help yourself is an imperative verb phrase; feel free to take is an adjective predicate.
stand out/catch the eye are verb predicates; be noticeable/be conspicuous are adjective predicates.
what’s the matter uses a noun phrase, what’s wrong an adjective complement, and what happened a verb; the accepted question set has no shared role.
none of someone’s business is a noun phrase; have nothing to do with someone is a verb clause.
have no choice but to / be forced to / be compelled to share a strong necessity function; classify as prompt-level semi-modal auxiliary.
bound/sure/certain to do are property/epistemic adjective predicates; modal-like meaning alone is insufficient to reclassify them as auxiliary.
be to / be supposed to / be expected to do share an expectation/obligation semi-modal function.
give me a break / you must be joking / are you kidding me are conventional standalone reactions expressing disbelief; classify their shared response function as interjection.
in front of / in someone’s presence head noun-phrase complements and function as prepositions.
pay attention to is a lexical verb phrase, while be mindful of is an adjective predicate. The answer set crosses roles.
as far as someone is concerned / when it comes to are clause frames, while as for is a prepositional phrase. The topic-setting meaning does not give one shared category.
be open to / be likely to are adjective predicates, while tend to cause is a lexical verb predicate. The accepted set crosses roles.
be inclined to is an adjective predicate, tend to is a lexical verb, and have a tendency to is noun-headed. The answer set has no shared role.
get along/get on are lexical verbs, while be on good terms is a predicative adjective phrase.
in tears is a prepositional state predicate, while crying is a progressive verbal predicate. The prompt does not disambiguate a common role.
be seeing/date/go out with are verb predicates, while be in a relationship with someone is noun-headed. The accepted set crosses roles.
what’s up / how have you been / how’s it going / what’s new are full interrogative clauses with different heads; the taxonomy has no question/sentence category.
be there for someone uses a locative complement, stand by/support are verb predicates, and have someone’s back is noun-headed. The answer set does not share a category.
shut up is a verb imperative, be quiet is an adjective predicate, and fall silent is verbal. The accepted set crosses categories.
go easy/give a break/cut slack are verb predicates, while be lenient is an adjective predicate. The answer set crosses roles.
to tell the truth / to be honest / honestly / frankly all function as sentence-level candor adjuncts (adverbial discourse markers).
after you / go ahead are standalone conventional yielding/permission responses; the taxonomy’s response-use interjection class captures their shared discourse function.
anything goes has the lexical verb go as its predicate and no paraphrases contradict that function.
no wonder is a conventional standalone reaction expressing that something is unsurprising.
not much / nothing much / nothing in particular are pronominal noun phrases in the elliptical reply use.
feel down / feel low / be depressed share a state adjective predicate; feel is copular in this meaning.
take your time / no rush / there’s no hurry are standalone reassuring permission responses; interjection is their shared discourse-response role.
relevant is an adjective, while relate to something is a lexical verb; be related to is participial/adjectival. The accepted set crosses roles.
familiar / be well versed / be knowledgeable are adjective predicates, while know something well is a lexical verb. The answer set crosses categories.
eager / be keen are adjective predicates, while long to / yearn to are lexical verbs. The accepted answer set crosses roles.
alarming is an adjective, while worry someone / make someone anxious are lexical verb predicates. Same causative meaning, different grammatical roles.
do you have the time? / what time is it? are reusable multi-slot interrogative templates asking for the current time; question function has no separate class.
differ is a lexical verb, while different is an adjective; the Japanese gloss does not resolve the accepted canonical/paraphrase split.
necessity / must-have are noun uses, while essential is an adjective. The Japanese “必需品” is nominal, but the allowed answer set includes adjective paraphrase essential.
resemble/look like are lexical verb predicates, while be similar to is an adjective predicate. The answer set crosses roles.
anxious/eager are adjective predicates, while long for/yearn for are lexical verbs. The prompt’s longing meaning does not create one shared role.
deserve is a lexical verb; be worth something and be worthy of something are adjective predicates. The answer set crosses roles.
alternative is an adjective in the prompt sense, while replacement/substitute are commonly nouns in this accepted set. The entry does not identify the intended syntactic use.
regret doing is a lexical verb construction, while be sorry about something is an adjective predicate. The prompt “後悔する” fits the canonical verb, but the accepted answer set crosses categories.
realize/notice are lexical verbs, whereas become aware of something is an adjective predicate. The answer set crosses roles.
be apt to / be prone to are adjective predicates, while tend to is a lexical verb. The propensity meaning is shared but the grammar category is not.
be entitled to is an adjective predicate; have the right to is a verb phrase with a noun complement. The prompt-level entitlement meaning does not make them one grammatical role.
be allowed/permitted to and have permission to all encode deontic permission as semi-modal expressions in this prompt-level function.
cannot/never do something too much is the degree/result-like multi-slot template; its paired word order is the target.
why don’t you / how about / what about + action are reusable suggestion templates, and the template itself is the target.
mind/dislike are lexical verbs, while be reluctant to is an adjective predicate. The accepted answer set crosses roles.
somewhat/to some extent are adverbial; some/a little can be determiners or pronouns. The Japanese gloss alone does not identify the intended syntactic use.
the end justifies the means is a complete declarative clause; by any means necessary is adverbial, and whatever it takes is a free relative clause. The answer set has no shared grammatical category.
not X but Y is a multi-slot contrast construction, while rather than/instead of are connector/preposition expressions. The accepted answer set crosses roles.
sore throat is a compound noun denoting the symptom.
in good spirits/in a good mood are predicative state complements, functioning adjectivally.
for here or to go / eat in or take away are multi-slot choice-question templates; the contrasting slots and order are the learning target.
be yet to / have yet to / have not ... yet share an incomplete/non-fulfillment aspectual auxiliary function.
from an objective viewpoint/perspective and objectively speaking all function as sentence-level viewpoint adjuncts.
resent is a lexical verb, while get angry/get mad are predicative adjective phrases. The accepted answer set crosses grammatical roles.
In every way/in every respect are manner/extent adjuncts.
After a while is a temporal adjunct.
Except for/apart from/other than head an excluding relation and take an NP complement.

There is little prospect that is an existential clause with a noun head; be unlikely to is an adjective predicate; have little chance of is a verb phrase with a noun complement. They express the same prompt meaning but do not share one of the taxonomy’s grammatical roles.
be anxious to and be dying to are adjective predicates, while can’t wait to is a lexical verb phrase with modal can. The accepted answer set crosses roles.
In itself/in and of itself/per se function as adverbial modifiers.
After all/in the end/ultimately function as sentence or clause adverbs.
be against something is a predicative adjective/prepositional complement, while oppose something and object to something are lexical verb phrases. The accepted answer set crosses roles.
somebody has the specified sense “important person”; the accepted VIP/key figure/big shot answers are noun phrases, so the prompt-level use is nominal.
be supposed to, be expected to, and be meant to share a deontic/expectation semi-modal function in this prompt.
what if it rains and what will you do if it rains are reusable multi-slot hypothetical-question templates.
I bet is a lexical verb clause expressing confident belief, while I’m sure is an adjective predicate. The accepted answer set expresses the same certainty meaning but crosses grammatical roles.
ought to and should express advice/obligation as modal or semi-modal auxiliaries.
whether or not and if introduce an embedded alternative/interrogative clause.
first of all and to begin with are sentence-organizing sequencing adjuncts.
make good/succeed/make it are lexical verb predicates, while be successful is an adjective predicate. The accepted answer set crosses roles.
the last person to do something / the least likely person to do something instantiate a reusable superlative likelihood template with an open action slot.
Otherwise functions as a conjunctive adverb, while if not introduces a conditional clause. The Japanese “そうでなければ” does not determine whether the target is a clause connector or an adverbial conjunct.
spontaneous is an adjective, while occur naturally/happen naturally are verb clauses. The answer set shares the notion of happening without external cause but not a grammatical category.
prolonged is an adjective/past participle modifier, while drag on/linger/persist are lexical verb predicates. The accepted set crosses roles.
The Japanese meaning explicitly includes both “呪い” (curse as a noun) and “呪う” (curse as a verb), and the entry accepts no alternatives that resolve the intended use.
Do you mind if I sit here / Can I / May I / Is it okay if I sit here are permission-request question templates.
Come on in both meanings is a conventional standalone urging/protest response.

can’t help it/can’t be helped contain modal auxiliary constructions, while there’s nothing you can do is a complete existential clause. The prompt alone does not establish one shared grammatical role.
I wish I could is a multi-slot wish template with an elliptical infinitive recoverable from context.
I’d be glad/happy/love to and with pleasure are conventional affirmative response formulas.
a series of / a sequence of introduce a quantified noun complement and function as determiner-like quantity expressions in the prompt.
with a view to doing something is a prepositional phrase, while to do/in order to/so as to introduce infinitival purpose clauses. They share an adjunct meaning but not a grammatical category.
on the verge of/on the brink of take an NP complement and express a state boundary.
be due to and be caused by are predicative adjective/participle phrases, while result from and stem from are lexical verb phrases. The accepted answer set crosses roles.
be related/connected/associated to are adjective predicates, while have something to do with is a lexical verb phrase. The accepted answer set crosses roles.
be rich in is an adjective predicate, while abound in is a lexical verb predicate. The accepted set crosses roles.
be similar to is an adjective predicate, while resemble is a lexical verb. The accepted set crosses roles.
be characteristic of/be unique to/be peculiar to are all predicative adjective phrases under the Japanese relationship meaning.
below and under can be adverbs without a complement or prepositions taking an NP; the Japanese “下に” and listed alternatives do not establish whether the target use includes a complement.
tens of thousands of is a multiword quantity expression selecting a noun complement.
so what?/what of it? are standalone dismissive challenge/reaction forms.
a bunch of/a lot of/many express quantity and select a noun complement in this prompt.
from coast to coast/across the country function as spatial extent adjuncts.
be sure to do something is an adjective predicate, while make sure to do something is a lexical verb phrase. The accepted answer set expresses certainty/ensuring but crosses roles.
per day/a day express a rate per temporal unit and function as a prepositional rate adjunct.
with + NP + participial complement is an open-slot absolute construction.
the comparative proposition alternatives share a reusable superlative comparison template.
for free/free of charge function as manner or cost adjuncts.
at least expresses a lower bound on degree/quantity.
three times as large as mine is an adjective phrase, while three times the size of mine is an NP predicate. The answer set does not share one grammatical category.

I’m afraid is an adjective clause, unfortunately is an adverb, and I think is a lexical verb clause. These stance markers share the sentence-level meaning “it is unfortunate that…”, but not one grammatical category.
owe is a lexical verb, while be indebted to someone is an adjective predicate. The accepted answer set crosses roles.
I mean is a lexical verb clause used as a reformulation marker, while in other words/that is are adverbial discourse markers. The Japanese “つまり” does not select one shared category.
on/upon doing and immediately after doing all use a preposition with a gerundial or temporal complement.
what do you do/what do you do for a living/what is your job are reusable occupation-question templates.
what is your major/what are you majoring in are reusable field-of-study question templates.
as soon as/the moment connect a temporal subordinate clause to a main clause.
find it hard to adjust/have difficulty adjusting/struggle to adjust all function as lexical verb predicates.
owe someone something is a lexical verb construction, while be indebted to someone for something is an adjective predicate. The accepted answer set crosses roles.
decade is a noun, while for ten years is a prepositional duration phrase used adverbially. The prompt meaning and answer set do not select one shared grammatical category.
used to do expresses past habitual/state aspect as a quasi-modal and is grouped with auxiliary in this taxonomy.
it is the case/true that is an open-slot extraposition/focus template.
dare to do is a lexical verb meaning to have the courage to do something in this prompt.
numerous is an adjective, while many and a large number of function as quantity determiners. The Japanese prompt identifies quantity but not a shared syntactic category.
reign is specified as both “統治・治世” (noun) and “君臨する” (verb), while rule is accepted as a verb; the entry combines nominal and verbal uses.
resolution and solution are nouns, while resolve is a lexical verb. The Japanese meaning spans determination/resolution senses and the accepted set crosses roles.
pro-choice is an adjective, while support abortion rights is a lexical verb phrase. The accepted answer set crosses grammatical roles.
might as well do A as do B / would rather do A than do B share a multi-slot comparative preference template.
throughout/all over express a spatial relation with a location complement.
hesitate to do is a lexical verb predicate, while be reluctant to do is an adjective predicate. The accepted answer set crosses grammatical roles.

instead of/in place of/in lieu of are prepositional expressions, while rather than can function as a conjunction connecting clauses or constituents. The prompt does not resolve the complement structure.

three in five/three out of five can be a quantified noun phrase or a determiner/pronominal numeral depending on whether a following noun is supplied. The Japanese fraction prompt gives no syntactic context.
be about to/be on the verge of doing share a prompt-level imminent-action quasi-modal function.
a pile of/a lot of/heaps of/loads of quantify a following noun.
according to introduces a source/basis complement.
offensive is an adjective meaning causing offense, while offend is a lexical verb. The accepted answer set crosses roles.
be bound for and be headed for are adjective/participle predicates, while be on one’s way to is a prepositional predicate. The shared destination meaning does not yield one role.

it won’t be long before everything is ready is a reusable clause template; everything will be ready soon is a declarative verb clause with a sentence-level adverb. The answer set does not share one grammar category.
turn around/look back are multiword lexical verbs in the specified “振り向く” sense.
from generation to generation/for generations/generation after generation function as temporal adjuncts.
access to something denotes the ability/right of use and functions as a noun phrase.

twenty-something can be an attributive adjective or a nominal label for a person in their twenties; in one’s twenties is a prepositional phrase. The Japanese gloss does not specify the syntactic environment.
delight is a noun, while be delighted/be overjoyed/be thrilled are adjective predicates. The answer set crosses roles.
be good/skilled at doing something are adjective predicates, while excel at doing something is a lexical verb. The accepted answer set crosses roles.
be afraid/be scared are adjective predicates, while fear doing something is a lexical verb. The accepted answer set crosses roles.
even though/although/though introduce clauses as conjunctions, while despite/in spite of take noun or gerund complements as prepositions. The accepted answer set crosses categories.

cover your mouth is an imperative verb phrase, while with a hand over one’s mouth is a prepositional phrase. The Japanese context gives the action but the accepted answers do not share a grammar category.
congratulations/congrats are standalone conventional felicitation reactions.
you’re welcome/no problem/my pleasure/don’t mention it/not at all are conventional response formulas.
see you later/see you function as conventional standalone farewells.
between you and me/just between us are parenthetical confidential-aside adjuncts.
how come/why are interrogative adverbs asking for a reason.
that’s too bad/I’m sorry to hear that are conventional sympathy responses.
I’m sorry/that’s a shame are conventional standalone sympathy responses.
you know is an attention-getting/discourse filler in the specified use.
let’s see/well/um/let me see are standalone hesitation/filler responses.
